clue.text: Hope abandoned, live in a satellite

indicators.note: abandoned suggests letters let loose and running wild, so the word Hope is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
to live is to be, to exist

explanation.surface: Someone gives up hope and goes to live on a moon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hope abandoned' reads as despair, but 'abandoned' is the anagram signal working on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoebe is one of the moons of Saturn, a natural satellite.

clue.text: Seasoned and made perfect by a saw?

explanation.surface: Wood seasoned and trued with a saw.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'saw' is not a tool but a saying: 'practice makes perfect'.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasoned means experienced; the proverb says repetition brings skill, so the skill it brings is a saying's work.

clue.text: Scotch governor has a large opener for this kind of glass

parts.note: an optic is the measuring device fixed to an upturned bottle of whisky, regulating each shot

indicators.note: opener asks for only the opening letter of the word large

explanation.surface: Someone with a big bottle opener for a whisky glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener' looks like a bottle opener; it means the first letter of 'large'. An optic is the pub measure on a spirits bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenses, spectacles and microscope glass are glass made for seeing.

clue.text: Dart thrown at bull by beginner in a bar led to riot

indicators.note: led to riot means these letters run wild into a new order

parts.note: L is a learner, a beginner, as on a learner driver's plate
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A bullfight dart, and a novice in a bar who started a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: L (the learner's plate) joins IN A BAR LED, and 'to riot' rearranges all ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In bullfighting a banderillero plants barbed decorated darts in the bull's neck.

clue.text: Only scraps left, the demonic S. Todd having taken chaps in

indicators.note: having taken chaps in means the rearranged letters hold another piece inside them
demonic means wild and frenzied, so the letters of S. Todd are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Sweeney Todd, the demon barber, has had men in and only scraps remain.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweeney Todd is the murderous barber of Victorian melodrama, so 'demonic' reads as a description of him; it is the anagram signal, and 'having taken ... in' splits round 'chaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Leftover odds and ends are the scraps remaining after the main part is used.

clue.text: Paper said to come out and die out

indicators.note: to come out suggests the letters of paper said break free and reform

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A newspaper reports something has emerged and then faded away.
explanation.definitionFit: To die out is to vanish, to cease to exist or be seen.

clue.text: No single strain in this spinning-machine?

explanation.surface: A question about a spinning machine that copes with no single yarn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strain' looks like stress on a thread; it is a breed. A mule is a hybrid of donkey and horse, and also Crompton's spinning machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A hybrid animal is of no single breed; Samuel Crompton's machine for spinning cotton bears the same name.

clue.text: Len caught out, perhaps, as great bat

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged differently

parts.note: taken as written
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
taken as written

explanation.surface: Batsman Len is caught out, perhaps, which is a great bat's fate.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface has Len caught out as a great batsman; the 'bat' is the flying mammal.
explanation.definitionFit: The noctule is one of Europe's largest bats, a big brown species.

clue.text: Determined to get records raised

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: notes are written records

explanation.surface: Determined to see recordings raised.
explanation.definitionFit: Being set on doing something means being resolved or intent on it.

clue.text: Black spot for blue material

explanation.surface: A dark mark on blue fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' here means indecent, not the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A sooty particle or fungal blotch is a black mark; obscene writing or pictures are filthy matter.

clue.text: Triumvir Mark's first contrary term?

parts.note: Mark Antony was one of the Second Triumvirate of Rome

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word Mark's

explanation.surface: A question about what Mark Antony's first opposing word was.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface runs 'Triumvir Mark' together as Mark Antony, but 'Triumvir' gives his surname alone and 'Mark's first' gives M.
explanation.definitionFit: A word of opposite meaning is a contrary term, as hot is to cold.

clue.text: To canvass is very good — and legal!

parts.note: so can mean very, as in so kind
licit describes what is permitted and lawful, both proper and legal

explanation.surface: An exclamation that canvassing is not only worthwhile but within the law.
explanation.definitionFit: To canvass is to seek votes or custom by asking people directly, to petition them.

clue.text: Kind of welcome in New York that comes from the heart-string

definitions.text: Kind of welcome in New York

parts.note: ticker is slang for the heart
tape is a narrow strip, like string

explanation.surface: A heartfelt welcome in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'heart-string' suggests sentiment; split it into 'heart' and 'string'.
explanation.definitionFit: New York greets heroes with parades showered in paper streamers, once ribbons from stock-price machines.

clue.text: Boy left behind when Maria leaves the joint

indicators.note: Maria leaves means the letters of that name are taken out of the longer word

parts.note: a joint is a cannabis cigarette, so the joint stands for its drug
taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: A boy is left behind when Maria walks out of the nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the joint' looks like a nightclub; it is a cannabis cigarette. Taking M, A, R, I, A out of the drug's name leaves a Spanish boy's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Juan is a Spanish given name for a boy, the equivalent of John.

clue.text: In double-Dutch style?

parts.note: Dutch is old slang for a wife, so having a double helping of one is marrying twice over

explanation.surface: Talking in incomprehensible gibberish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double-Dutch' means gibberish, but 'Dutch' is Cockney slang for a wife (from 'duchess'), so double Dutch is two wives at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Being married to two spouses at once is the crime of having two wives.

clue.text: Serving subject of a terrible hard life

definitions.text: Serving subject of a terrible hard life

parts.words: Serving subject of a terrible hard life
parts.note: a subject of the Crown who is serving in the ranks, enduring a famously tough existence

explanation.surface: A loyal subject in service, enduring a dreadful, hard existence.
explanation.definitionFit: A private in the army is a subject serving the Crown, with a life of hardship and danger.

clue.text: Retired man on the way up has to turn back

indicators.note: on the way up in a down clue means the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Trevor is a man's name

explanation.surface: A retired man with a career on the rise has to turn back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' looks like the reversal signal; it is the abbreviation RET. 'on the way up' turns TREVOR into ROVERT.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrovert is to tilt or turn backwards, a medical term for organs.

clue.text: Patent I had used in the outcome

indicators.note: used in means one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: an event can mean an outcome, as in in the event
I had shortens to I'd

explanation.surface: An inventor's patent applied in the final result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patent' looks like an inventor's licence, but here it is the adjective meaning obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent as an adjective means plain and obvious, clear to see.

clue.text: Peg formally raised to introduce first of toasts — say "Skol"?

indicators.note: to introduce means the reversed name takes another letter into it
raised in a down clue means the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Peg is a nickname for Margaret, its formal version

indicators.note: first of asks for only the opening letter of the word toasts

explanation.surface: Peg, raising her glass to propose the first toast, says Skol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns MARGARET into TERAGRAM, and T from 'toasts' goes in. 'Skol', the Scandinavian toast, is defined by example as a word of four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Any word of four letters is a four-letter word, and the toast Skol is one such word.

clue.text: Spot doctor with work-permit?

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: A doctor checking for spots, armed with a work permit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work-permit' reads as one document, but the hyphen hides two separate pieces, and 'Spot' is a noun for a small drop, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot of liquid is a tiny drop of it.

clue.text: This Japanese art is increasing, we hear

definitions.text: This Japanese art is increasing, we hear

parts.words: This Japanese art is increasing, we hear
parts.note: the paper craft is all about folding, and folding sounds like the suffix of growth in twofold or manifold

explanation.surface: A report that a Japanese art is growing in popularity.
explanation.walkthrough: The Japanese art is folding paper; 'increasing' plays on '-fold' (twofold, tenfold), so the art is 'folding' in both senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese craft of paper folding makes figures from single sheets.

clue.text: Computer information not kept secret

explanation.surface: Computer data that has been leaked.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer's displayed or printed output is its data; something announced aloud is no longer private.

clue.text: Ham finished before work?

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the second

parts.note: something finished is over
an act is a deed, a piece of work

explanation.surface: A ham actor done for before the work starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham' is a verb here, to act too theatrically.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to perform in an exaggerated, theatrical way.

clue.text: Fast-talking party following introduction of Gallup

indicators.note: following means the party is placed after the opening letter
introduction of asks for only the opening letter of the word Gallup

parts.note: Lib is short for the Liberal party

explanation.surface: A slick party spokesman after a Gallup poll is introduced.
explanation.walkthrough: Gallup is the opinion-poll company, which suits the political surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth, fast-talking speaker is facile and superficial in speech.

clue.text: Peach in pot?

explanation.surface: A peach in a plant pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peach' is the old verb to inform on someone; 'pot' is cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: To peach means to inform on, British slang to grass; pot is cannabis, which is also called weed.

clue.text: Western bay sheltering HMS Pinafore, for example

parts.note: a bay is a reddish-brown horse
HMS Pinafore is a comic opera by Gilbert and Sullivan

explanation.surface: A western bay where the warship HMS Pinafore takes shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bay' looks like a stretch of coast for a ship; it is a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy film is jokingly called by this name, likening it to melodramatic stage drama.

clue.text: Owing money in South Africa can weaken the spirit

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: OD is the banking abbreviation for overdrawn, owing money

explanation.surface: Debt in South Africa can sap the national morale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' looks like morale; it is whisky, which soda water dilutes.
explanation.definitionFit: Fizzy water mixed into whisky or brandy dilutes the drink.

clue.text: Steady business

explanation.surface: A stable company.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady means solid and unshaken; a company or business concern shares the same short word.

clue.text: Mineral for stomach, say?

indicators.note: say tells us the word is to be spoken, giving a word of similar sound

parts.note: stomach for something is appetite for it

explanation.surface: A question whether a mineral is good for the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Apatite is a phosphate mineral, the main source of phosphorus for fertiliser.

clue.text: Wildly praised as a literary giant

indicators.note: wildly means the letters of praised are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone extravagantly acclaimed as a great author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'literary giant' looks like a great author; it is Giant Despair, the ogre of Doubting Castle in Bunyan's The Pilgrim's Progress.
explanation.definitionFit: In Bunyan's allegory a giant of hopelessness imprisons Christian and Hopeful in Doubting Castle.

clue.text: Hearty pastime, possibly, round hospital

indicators.note: round means the rearranged letters go around the other piece
possibly suggests the letters of pastime might be arranged otherwise

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A hearty hobby, perhaps, played around a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearty' looks like an adjective; it is the old nautical noun for a sailor, as in 'me hearties'. 'possibly' rearranges PASTIME around H.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors address their fellow crew as hearties, so a hearty is a sailing companion.

clue.text: Orderliness of Topsy's temperament

indicators.note: of signals that the letters come out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Tidiness as part of a girl named Topsy's character.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across Topsy's and temperament.
explanation.definitionFit: Order and method in doing things is having a method or regular scheme.
